learnings.title: HO-05 Shopify: first five secret-free preparation steps
learnings.claim: Without a Shopify store token, public official Shopify documentation can establish API field requirements, analytics definitions, rate limits, and safe read-only planning, but cannot reveal the user's live shop data or cohort metrics.
learnings.decision: Do the following five steps without secret or live store writes; only then request read-only store access if truly needed.

steps.action: Create a read-only GraphQL field checklist for products, variants, inventory, orders, customers, and analytics; label required scopes and API version.
Define cohort metrics (first vs returning customers, repeat purchase rate) and prevent unsupported claims about attribution.
Prepare a product-opportunity scoring template: demand, landed cost, shipping, return risk, gross/net margin, and evidence confidence; no live shop assumptions.
Write a public-docs-based GraphQL query skeleton with minimal fields and cursor pagination, but do not execute against store or request credentials.
Specify rate-limit-aware retries and a dry-run validation fixture; 401/403 must block rather than retry repeatedly.

learnings.next_measurement: Review the field checklist against current Admin GraphQL API version; verify real Shopify connection/scopes before any actual query; measure first read-only dry run and record evidence.
failure_history: No live Shopify store query or customer/order data was accessed in this task.
fallback_history: If store read scope unavailable, retain templates and report BLOCKED_EXTERNAL instead of invented metrics.
